precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 9:9
precepts.why:
“It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him.” A help meet is someone to help him through his daily chores and through living, something to his liking, something for him. God first brought every beast and fowl to Adam, and Adam named them all, because he was over them. Then it says, “but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him.” Nothing yet was just for him.

So “the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam”, took one of his ribs, “made he a woman, and brought her unto the man.” This is the Most High doing this for his son, and that is a gift. The gift still remains today for every man. That is why we call her your rib: there is a woman made just for you, because it is not good for man to be alone.

Solomon says what to do with that gift: “Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun”. Living joyfully takes application. It is something you have to make happen.

He goes on: “for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun.” God made this woman for you. She is the portion you have been given in this life and in all the work you do under the sun, so receive her as the gift she is and live joyfully with her.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 11:8-9
precepts.why:
Adam said, “This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.” Just as Adam had dominion over the creatures he named, he named her. So there is no confusion about why the woman was made, Paul says: “For the man is not of the woman; but the woman of the man.” “Neither was the man created for the woman; but the woman for the man.”

People debate and say we all come from the woman, so how can the man be over her? They do not know the Bible. The woman came from the man. That is thus saith the Lord; argue with God. God created the woman for the man, and nobody can create or remake their own purpose in life.

So many people, men and women, spend their lives fighting against their God-given purpose. It is self-sabotage: you will destroy your whole house trying to be something you are not. And you wonder why you are dealing with spirits of depression and anxiety and always on edge: it is because you are fighting against your God-given role. You cannot change it, and trying only brings confusion.

Out of all the beasts of the field there was nothing fit for the man, so God made him a woman, and that woman has a purpose: help meet for her husband. Sometimes the help starts to think she is the purpose, that she is the house. No: you are the help meet for me and my house. The sooner you accept the truth, the sooner there will be peace in your home and peace within yourself; turmoil comes when you leave that place.

That is where it all went left. Eve knew the rule, but the serpent spoke to what was already within her: “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She wanted the position that was over her. Paul goes back to the beginning for the same reason: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve.” “And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” And Sirach says, “Of the woman came the beginning of sin, and through her we all die.” All she had to do was stay in her role and in order.

You might think it too far-fetched that your beloved wife, the mother of your children, the woman who takes care of you, could have the goddamn devil over you while you sleep. But the first woman, the first created by God himself, was susceptible to the devil. You think your wife ain't? That is why the head has to keep reminding them of their place and role in the home.

precepts.label: Genesis 3:16
precepts.why:
“I will make him an help meet for him.” To help is to give assistance or support to someone, to provide something useful or necessary in achieving an end. Meet means suitable for him. So the help is the one who assists in making what the husband wants happen. Sometimes the help thinks she is supposed to lead, or thinks she is supposed to guide, but that is not what a help is.

Genesis 3:16 comes after the transgression: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Some have taken this to mean it was only at this point that the woman was supposed to listen to her husband. No. She was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the fall.

So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing? Sisters, the help is the greatest thing you are ever going to be. The moment you decide being the help is not the greatest thing you can be, or think you are supposed to be something outside of the help, you are going to destroy your marriage.

It cuts both ways. Brothers, the moment you decide not to provide, not to leave the house and work, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household: your marriage will crumble and your life will be in shambles. It is a domino effect. And headship is maintenance, a routine thing a husband has to keep doing. A wife will never say she is trying to overthrow you, but it is in her spirit, the same way a man wants to do things his own way when he gets orders from those ranked above him. So you will have to remind her: I am the head, you have to listen to me.

precepts.label: Isaiah 3:12
precepts.why:
Write this down: women were never designed to lead men. God made the woman “an help meet” for the man, and when that order is turned around, Isaiah 3:12 calls it what it is: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.”

That is a curse. It is not a good thing; it shows things out of order, not how God set it up. A woman's body alone shows she was not made to lead men into danger: her cycle comes, she is pregnant for nine months, and she is supposed to lead you somewhere?

Women ruling over you is a curse, brothers. Some of you are scared to lead your house and have let her lead. If you are passive, scared, afraid of confrontation, she is going to walk all over you. It is not a secret; everyone sees it, and other men see it in your demeanor. You have to change the way you think. Stand up and take your place back.

The women were designed to be a help to their husbands. When they step outside of that, and when the brothers allow it, chaos follows. That is why there is dysfunction in our nation right now: because the men do not want to lead.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 31:22
precepts.why:
“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” A new thing: women being over men was never heard of. It is not natural, and it is not the natural state of a man to be run by a woman. But you allow it.

God did not set it up that way. In Genesis 2 he made the woman a help meet for the man. When she compasses him instead, the order is upside down.

Cases come up where a brother does not know what is going on in his own house. His wife pays all the bills while he is on the couch playing video games, and he cannot understand why his home is in confusion. It is because his wife is running things. She has been the breadwinner from day one, so she looks at it as normal, and he is used to it. He did not want a wife; he wanted a mama.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 34:31
precepts.why:
“And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.” The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. You will not change the order of things just because you are weak, or scared of your wife.

Sisters, the beta men on social media are influencing you, making you think the man is supposed to worship the ground you walk on. That will not influence the men in purple and gold. We are not worried about being called names, narcissist or misogynist. The question is, do you want a man or do you want a boy?

When your husband gets around the brothers and comes home acting different, he is supposed to. He examines himself, sees he is lacking, and comes home on fire to fix his house, with a little more pep in his step and a little more to say. The same goes when he has been rebuked for adultery or for not dealing with his wife the right way: he is supposed to move different. It works in every area if he truly believes.

This is why there is an attack on the household. Satan and his people know that to destroy us they have to attack our foundation, and the foundation is the home. Paul warned that in the last days perilous times would come, with those “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”, and “of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” They get in through the phone and the conversations, whoever is influencing them. We are building a nation, and if we are not strong on the home front, we will not get off the ground.

precepts.label: Malachi 2:14
precepts.why:
In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:1
precepts.why:
“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 25:5-6
precepts.why:
About three months after Judah went in to Tamar, she began to show, and word came to Judah that his daughter-in-law had played the harlot and was with child by whoredom. Her husband was dead and she was living in her father's house, so Judah said, “Bring her forth, and let her be burnt”: that was the law for a harlot. But she sent him his own signet, bracelets and staff, and “Judah acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son.” The child was his, and he was the one in the wrong.

Deuteronomy 25 shows what Judah and Onan owed her. Moses recites this law later, but our forefathers already had knowledge of it through oral tradition passed down from Adam. “If brethren dwell together, and one of them die, and have no child, the wife of the dead shall not marry without unto a stranger: her husband’s brother shall go in unto her.” That is why it was wrong when Onan spilled his seed on the ground.

“the firstborn which she beareth shall succeed in the name of his brother which is dead, that his name be not put out of Israel.” To succeed in the name of the dead brother does not mean the child takes his actual name. It means the child inherits the dead man's possession, his land and his things, because he left no seed to inherit for him. The brother raises up a surrogate seed in honor of his dead brother, so the land stays in his brother's name and is not lost.

A brother who refuses is brought before the elders. His brother's wife shall “loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face”, saying, “So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother’s house.” And “his name shall be called in Israel, The house of him that hath his shoe loosed.” He carries that humiliation forever, because he would not love his neighbor as himself. That is why the history of Ruth is so important. It is not about Ruth, the Moabite heathen woman; y'all make it about her because y'all love heathens.

So Tamar was more righteous than Judah: she kept her dead husband's name alive when Judah withheld Shelah. From her came twins. Zarah put out his hand first and the midwife bound a scarlet thread on it, but he drew it back and his brother broke forth: “this breach be upon thee: therefore his name was called Pharez.” Pharez means a breach, and the line of the kings runs through him.

precepts.label: Genesis 43:32
precepts.why:
“And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.” Our forefathers hated Joseph and sold him into slavery. He gained status in Egypt, Egypt got through the famine by his counsel, and now his brothers came to Egypt to buy food.

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” If Joseph had been a German Jew, or from Holland, Ukraine or Poland, they would have known him: a white man in Egyptian clothes stands out among Egyptians, because the Egyptians are black. They could not recognize their brother because he was dressed in Egyptian garb, beard shaved, looking like an Egyptian. “for he spake unto them by an interpreter”: he acted the part, speaking Egyptian so they would not know him. Joseph passed for an African, a black man, just as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were dark ancestors.

Then Genesis 43:32, at the meal: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is Jim Crow. The Hebrews sat over there and the Egyptians over here, because them sitting together was an abomination. Israel had its own land, Goshen, and Egypt was apart. It was still segregation, even though both were dark: same color, different nation.

The pictures shown from the history books said the same. The Egyptians are brown. The Israelites working in the granary under a taskmaster have afros. Pharaoh is black, and Tutankhamun is black. Nefertiti is black as hell, and the Nubians are black as hell. The sacrifice of Isaac in the mosaic of the Beth Alpha synagogue shows Abraham and Isaac as black. The sons of Ham, the Egyptians, Canaanites, Nubians and Libyans, are all dark; we fought the Canaanites in the land, and they are black too.

Moses passed for an Egyptian the same way. Jethro's daughters said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. Moses married an Ethiopian woman, a daughter of Ham, and a Hamite would have known a white man was no Egyptian. Even Pharaoh's daughter knew the baby was a Hebrew only because he was circumcised, since both peoples were black.

thread.text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

precepts.label: Exodus 1:8
precepts.why:
“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”. This new king set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with burdens, and then went further: “And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive”.

That is gator bait. They sacrificed our baby boys in the river to Sobek, the gator god. The white man did the exact same thing to us in the Florida Everglades: put our babies in a net, wait for the alligator to bite, pull the gator out and make shoes and bags out of him. Egypt did it to us first. They killed the males and kept the women alive, because the women do not produce the nation; the man does.

That decree is why Moses was hidden three months and laid in an ark of bulrushes by the river's brink, and why everything that follows was done in secret. When Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river in Exodus 2:5 and found the ark, she found one of the very sons her father had ordered cast into the river.

precepts.label: Numbers 12:1
precepts.why:
When Pharaoh's daughter opened the ark, “she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children”. How did she know? He was circumcised. You never read about Moses getting circumcised; he was already cut, because some of our forefathers retained that custom from our fathers. Outside of that, she would not have known the difference, because Egyptians and Hebrews were both black.

Then Moses fled to Midian and helped the seven daughters of the priest of Midian at the well, and they told their father Reuel, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. What did they call Moses? An Egyptian. The same way Joseph's brothers took Joseph for an Egyptian. Reuel, Jethro, gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

Numbers 12:1 shows what that family was: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman”. She was Ethiopian, so Moses' father-in-law was an Ethiopian, a priest of Midian but not a Midianite. Ethiopians are children of Ham, Kushites, the family of the Egyptians. A Hamite would know a Hamite when he saw one, and they still took Moses for an Egyptian. If he had been a white man, they would have known he was no Egyptian.

Paul passed for one too: “Art not thou that Egyptian”, the chief captain asked, and Paul answered, “I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Moses passed for an Egyptian, Joseph passed for an Egyptian, Paul passed for an Egyptian. These are black people. That's the point.

precepts.label: Leviticus 19:3
precepts.why:
Respect is taught in childhood, and it starts with “Honour thy father and thy mother.” Leviticus says it the same way: “Ye shall fear every man his mother, and his father, and keep my sabbaths: I am the Lord your God.”

The Lord understands the importance of structure, and it has always been there. You are to fear every man his mother and his father, and that goes on into old age. Don't think that once you turn 20 you don't have to listen. That power is always there: you honour your father and your mother.

And wives, once you become someone's wife, you also have your husband to deal with. The same power a father has over his daughter is handed over to her husband when he gives her away, so the respect a child learns for father and mother is the first line of the respect a wife owes her husband. That is how honouring father and mother connects to a wife respecting her husband.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 5:16
precepts.why:
Moses repeats the commandment: “Honour thy father and thy mother, as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee; that thy days may be prolonged, and that it may go well with thee, in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

It was so important for them to honour their father and mother so that their days would be prolonged, so they would not die, and so it would go well with them in the land. The Lord knew from the beginning that the inner structure of the home is what builds the nation.

When there is dysfunction, anything not aligned with how God set it up, there are going to be problems, and it affects the whole nation. Certain households affect other households. If your house is out of order and you are best friends with so-and-so, your kids play together and learn the same bad behaviours. If a sister is a gossiper running from home to home and she is your wife's best friend, it is only a matter of time before your wife is called a gossiper too. Same with you: kick it with the murmurers and you will murmur.

You will infect the nation if your household is not in order. God is about order, always has been. A child raised in a household where the father and mother both understood the laws of God, operated within their roles and demanded obedience to God is more likely to carry that legacy on. Everybody still makes a choice, but the probability follows the household.

Peter and the apostles answered, “We ought to obey God rather than men”, and the mothers of the Maccabees did so to the death. Christ was hanged on a tree too; the King and his children have all hung under the same curse, until the Lord says enough.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:3
precepts.why:
“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?” We read it right there in the history of the slave ships.

Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What does Egypt represent? “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt is bondage. The Lord would bring us into bondage again, this time by way of ships; literal Egypt we would see no more again as a nation, and there we would be sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, slave men and slave women.

The Middle Passage, the Maafa, a massive disaster: for fifty days or more our people were packed in spaces as tight as coffins, a second platform barely twenty inches above the heads of those below, chained to the floor, lying in their own waste, amid rats that gnawed through wood and flesh, on floors covered with blood and excrement, where pregnant women gave birth and the living awoke chained to the dead. Tight packers crammed in as many as possible, reckoning the sales would offset the dead. The meal was horse beans pounded to a pulp with slabber sauce, once or twice a day, and a pint of water. Dumb negroes say it never happened and ask where the ships are: cargo ships carried spices and corn before us, carried us as cargo, and after slavery carried cargo again. Why get rid of them?

Then came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or forced our ancestors to beat out a rhythm while they jumped about, ankles rubbed raw by the leg irons, to keep the human cargo in salable condition. That is Psalms 137:3: those who carried us away captive required of us mirth. At night the cries rose; an enslaved woman explained the howling came from having dreamt they were in their own country and waking in the hold of a slave ship. A strange land indeed.

Millions were carried from Africa to the West Indies, North and South America and Europe, from Luanda, from the Congo, from Loango, where the old maps mark the Jews; the buyers and sellers both knew they were selling outsiders, not the same people. Deuteronomy 28:68 and Psalms 137:3 were fulfilled on those ships.

precepts.label: Judges 21:25
precepts.why:
Naomi told Ruth, “Behold, thy sister in law is gone back unto her people, and unto her gods”. Orpah went back to Moab, to her people and her gods. These were not Israelite women; this was a heathen woman of another nation. That is important, because there are doctrines out there teaching that Ruth was an Israelite. No, she was not. She was a heathen. Was it right for Boaz to deal with a heathen? No, but it happened.

Just in case there is any confusion, the last verse of Judges, right above Ruth, shows why it happened: “In those days there was no king in Israel: every man did that which was right in his own eyes.” During the judges, we did what we wanted to do.

And Ruth opens in that very time: “Now it came to pass in the days when the judges ruled”. There was no king. It was the time when Israel did what they wanted, and that included taking heathen women.

So Ruth's story does not make her an Israelite, and it does not make it right to take a heathen wife. It shows what Israel was doing when every man did what was right in his own eyes. The scripture keeps calling her what she is: “Ruth the Moabitess”. That is clear.

precepts.label: Zechariah 8:23
precepts.why:
Ruth said, “thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God”. She is a heathen saying, if I go with you, I will be as if I am an Israelite, and I will serve your God too. She is cleaving to an Israelite woman, that's all; there were no promises made to her. “Where thou diest, will I die, and there will I be buried”: I'm not leaving you.

The nations are going to be the same way in the kingdom. Zechariah shows it: “Thus saith the Lord of hosts; In those days it shall come to pass, that ten men shall take hold out of all languages of the nations, even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying, We will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.”

We will go with you, just like Ruth said. For we have heard that God is with you: your God is a real God, and ours is garbage. They are going to cleave to Israel the way Ruth cleaved to Naomi, and they will cleave as servants.

So Ruth is the picture of the nations in the kingdom: not Israelites, but holding on to Israel because the God of Israel is the true God.

precepts.label: John 4:3-5
precepts.why:
Ruth 4 is a trial at the gate before ten elders over land. Elimelech had land; he died, and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died too, leaving no man to take it. So the land had to be taken up by the next of kin. Boaz told the nearer kinsman that Naomi “selleth a parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.” A parcel of land: that phrase opens the whole chapter.

John 4 uses the same wording. Christ “must needs go through Samaria. Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.” Jacob gave Joseph that parcel of ground; he bought his son that land.

A parcel of land, a parcel of ground, a parcel of a field: they are all the same thing, and a parcel of land and an inheritance are one and the same. So when Boaz bought the parcel that was Elimelech's, he was not making an ordinary purchase. He was taking up an inheritance in Israel, one that had to stay in the family of the dead.

precepts.label: Genesis 33:18-20
precepts.why:
Genesis 33 gives the history behind the “parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph” in John 4. “Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan–aram; and pitched his tent before the city. And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.”

Jacob bought that land from the Hamites for a hundred pieces of money, and “he erected there an altar, and called it El–elohe–Israel.” A parcel of a field is again the same thing as a parcel of land: an inheritance.

Later, as he was dying, Israel told Joseph, “Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.” His sons did take the land by the sword; Simeon and Levi went crazy and killed the men of that city. But the field was bought first, before his sons ever took it. So the inheritance at Shechem stood on a lawful purchase, the same way Boaz bought Elimelech's parcel before the elders at the gate.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:32
precepts.why:
“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver: and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.” The parcel of ground, the parcel of land, the parcel of a field is the land of inheritance, and this one was given to Ephraim.

That is what Boaz was protecting in Ruth 4. The nearer kinsman would not redeem it, “lest I mar mine own inheritance”, and plucked off his shoe; here the shoe is passed without shame, because he is yielding the right to someone else, not refusing his brother. Boaz bought all that was Elimelech's, Chilion's and Mahlon's, and took Ruth, the wife of Mahlon, “to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance, that the name of the dead be not cut off from among his brethren.” The son he raised up would inherit that land, because it belonged to Mahlon. Boaz is still the father; Boaz begat Obed, and the line goes through Boaz. There are no two fathers. The land falls under the dead man's line; the lineage goes back to Boaz. That is love your neighbor as yourself.

So Elimelech did not lose his land. We kept our land in house. Land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your children; don't sell it off. Our people once had millions of acres in America, and Esau made laws, eminent domain among them, and found a distant kin to pay off with a little money, and so stole millions of acres, beaches included, from Judah.

The allotment still stands. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land, and Judges says “the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” Those families are here today. The Lord says he “will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” Whoever is left after the destruction, those who repent, will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 12:15
precepts.why:
“And Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed”. Boaz raised up seed in the name of Mahlon, but the record says Boaz begat Obed, not Mahlon, because Mahlon was dead. The genealogy goes under Boaz; the land falls under the dead man's line. Obed takes on the land of Elimelech even though that is not his father's line. That is the inheritance: the parcel of land, the parcel of field, the parcel of ground. You don't inherit a tribe; you inherit the land. And they were both of the same tribe anyway.

That is why the scripture says this in Jeremiah: “And it shall come to pass, after that I have plucked them out I will return, and have compassion on them, and will bring them again, every man to his heritage, and every man to his land.” It literally means what it says. In the beginning God allotted every family land.

The line of David had an inheritance given to it; the families of Judah each had land appointed to them. Guess what? Those families are here today. When the Lord returns, those that make it, that repented, are going back to that land, every man to his heritage.

That is why Boaz raised up seed for Elimelech's family: so the land would stay within that family's inheritance. That is loving your neighbor as yourself. We kept our land in house. So land is very important: if you have it, keep it and give it to your kids; don't just sell it off. A lot of Judah had millions of acres here in America, and Esau stole them, creating laws like eminent domain and finding some distant kin to pay a little money and take the land. There are beaches that belong to us. But the Lord will bring every man again to his heritage and to his land.

precepts.label: Judges 2:6
precepts.why:
Judges shows how the land was first given: “And when Joshua had let the people go, the children of Israel went every man unto his inheritance to possess the land.” We all had land and an inheritance. When we came out of Egypt, every family was allotted land. Whoever of those same families is left after the destruction takes place will be given back the land and inheritance that was given to us back then.

Notice it says every man unto his inheritance. Sisters, you're divorcing us and taking half our stuff, but it says every man. Our wives benefit from our inheritance; it belongs to the men, but it is theirs too because they are married to us. According to God, the inheritance belongs to the men, just as the earth belonged to Adam, and Eve benefitted from it because she was helping him.

And the land we inherit is not an acre or something. 1 Chronicles 2 shows Jair “who had three and twenty cities in the land of Gilead”, “even threescore cities”. We owned cities. Somebody literally owned the Bronx, Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens. We had castles on those cities, winter houses and summer houses.

That is why the land in Ruth had to stay with Elimelech's family. Boaz begat Obed, and the genealogy goes through Boaz down to Jesse and David, but the inheritance, every man's portion from the time of Joshua, stayed with the dead man's line through the seed raised up to him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:1
precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:11
precepts.why:
“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

precepts.label: 2 Samuel 14:25
precepts.why:
“But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.” Beauty became part of Absalom's identity. It was synonymous with him: his hair, his physical perfection.

And what came behind that? Ambition and rebellion. You get a big head about yourself and you start to believe certain things. Absalom rose up against his father, it came to civil war, and he died hanging from that very hair, the same thing that was vanity to him.

That is the same lesson as David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. David saw a woman “very beautiful to look upon”, he saw her, he inquired, and he took her, the same pattern as Shechem with Dinah. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house the rest of his days. The Lord forgave him, but he left him with drama for moving that way. Then Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty, came to pride and rebellion.

Whenever physical attraction becomes the forefront of anything, the Bible shows you that trouble comes behind it. Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage: she look good, I got to marry her so I can have her. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if that is the only thing you are moving on.

precepts.label: Proverbs 6:25
precepts.why:
This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The scripture teaches you not to lust after her beauty, and it says where: in thy heart, in thy mind.

“neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” She gives you the look back. You make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, the tentacles of auras come out and they embrace, and you done lost your mind. I got to have her. Bring me that. That's what I want.

That is exactly what happened to David in 2 Samuel 11:2. He walked on the roof, saw a woman washing herself, “and the woman was very beautiful to look upon”, and he moved on what he saw. Shechem saw Dinah and took her, and it ended in violence and massacre. Samson went after the one who pleased him well, and it ended in betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty, had to have her, and it ended in adultery and murder.

So Solomon's warning is the guard against the very thing David fell into: do not let the beauty get into your heart, and do not let the eyes take you. Attraction is not the foundation, and a man who moves on it alone gives up his strength.

precepts.label: Proverbs 7:10
precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She is trying to entice, and you fall for it. It works.

Here Solomon warns about being captured by appearance. How does he know these things? He said not one out of a thousand of the women he dealt with. He knew, and he probably knew before the thousandth. It goes to show how intoxicating it can be. You get caught up.

That is the thread through David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. Shechem saw Dinah and took her: violence and massacre. Samson, she pleased him well: betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty and had to have her: adultery and murder. Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty: pride and rebellion. And the strange women, being beautiful, lead to ruin.

That is why the Bible rarely makes much of the beauty of wives. Rebecca is known for her character, her hospitality and her faith; Zipporah's beauty is never described; Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted in our foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The Bible doesn't deny attraction; it just isn't the foundation.

precepts.label: 2 Kings 25:27-28
precepts.why:
Zedekiah rebelled like his brother and his nephew did. He tried to run away and got caught in the plains of Jericho, and they killed his kids in front of him first, then took his eyes out, bound him and locked him up in Babylon. At this point there are no more kings of Judah; Zedekiah was the last one. His sons are gone, his heirs are gone. So who's left?

Read on: “in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah”, “Evil–merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison; And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon”. Jehoiachin had been locked up between 36 and 37 years. Then he “changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.” His allowance was a continual allowance, a daily rate for every day: Babylon gave him a job and status.

Jehoiachin is Jeconiah, and he is the Jechonias of Matthew 1:11. He got some mercy in captivity, but was he a king anymore at this point? No. He was a king, but now he was a captive in Babylon, receiving wages and some status.

And in Babylon he had children: “the sons of Jeconiah; Assir, Salathiel his son”. Salathiel is Shealtiel, the father of Zerubbabel, whose name means born in Babylon. That is where the line of the kings of Judah went on after Zedekiah's sons were slain: through a captive king in Babylon.

precepts.label: 1 Kings 4:31
precepts.why:
Judah had five sons: Er, Onan and Shelah by the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess, and the twins Pharez and Zerah by Tamar. “The sons of Pharez; Hezron, and Hamul. And the sons of Zerah; Zimri, and Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara: five of them in all.” Ethan, Heman, Calcol and Dara became very famous. They were very wise.

How wise? Solomon’s wisdom is measured against them: “For he was wiser than all men; than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Chalcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol: and his fame was in all nations round about.”

Those same sons of Judah were so wise that many men were named after them, and Solomon surpassed even them. He was wiser than the wise men of his own tribe.

That is the house this genealogy runs through. Hezron, the oldest son of Pharez, begat Ram, and from Ram comes Amminadab, Nahshon, Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: a tribe of wise men, princes and kings.

precepts.label: Numbers 2:3
precepts.why:
“And Ram begat Amminadab; and Amminadab begat Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah”. Nahshon was of the elite princes of Judah, a prince family, a royal family. The census confirms the same man: “Of Judah; Nahshon the son of Amminadab.”

And in the camp: “And on the east side toward the rising of the sun shall they of the standard of the camp of Judah pitch throughout their armies: and Nahshon the son of Amminadab shall be captain of the children of Judah.”

So Nahshon was a captain. These men had serious status: princes and captains, leaders. They were warriors; they were not regular men.

“And Nahshon begat Salma, and Salma begat Boaz, And Boaz begat Obed, and Obed begat Jesse”. Boaz came from that line, the line of Pharez, the twin that breached, not the one whose hand came out first with the scarlet thread. And Jesse had eight sons, and one of those sons is David.

precepts.label: Exodus 6:23
precepts.why:
Now a tie-in regarding family ties: “And Aaron took him Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab, sister of Naashon, to wife; and she bare him Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.”

Aaron is Moses’ brother, of Levi. He took Elisheba, Amminadab’s daughter and Nahshon’s sister, to wife. Aaron’s wife was of the tribe of Judah. Those families intermarried, priests and kings marrying together. It is no coincidence; that is why John the Baptist and Christ are cousins.

Nadab and Abihu were the two who offered strange fire and were killed; Eleazar and Ithamar were spared. Eleazar became the high priest in the days of Joshua, the mediator before the Lord. So Eleazar’s mama was Judah. That is why some Levites don’t have the big heads; their mama is Judah. And don’t forget the big nose, too.

So Amminadab begat Nahshon and a daughter Elisheba. Aaron married Elisheba and had the four sons, the high priests, which makes Nahshon Aaron’s brother-in-law. And from Nahshon came Salma, Boaz, Obed and Jesse: the priesthood and the royal line of Judah bound together in one family.

precepts.label: Genesis 15:3-4
precepts.why:
Abram, childless, was going to leave his house to Eliezer of Damascus, the eldest servant born in his house: “Behold, to me thou hast given no seed: and, lo, one born in my house is mine heir.” The Lord said no: “This shall not be thine heir; but he that shall come forth out of thine own bowels shall be thine heir.” Not a heathen servant, but his own seed. An heir and an inheritance are the same word, like a family heirloom passed down the line.

That is the key to 1 Chronicles 2: “Now Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. And Sheshan had a servant, an Egyptian, whose name was Jarha. And Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife.” This was while Israel was in Egypt, when we had no land of inheritance allotted to us. People read it and say the Egyptian married into the tribe and became Judah. No.

The record follows that line for generation after generation so that it is known. When Israel came out of Egypt and inherited the land, that line could not receive land, because the land passes by the paternal bloodline and that line goes back to an Egyptian servant. They were among us in the land, but they did not inherit. It is written there to exclude, not to include. Sheshan's brothers had sons and received land; his line did not. It does not mean the Egyptian became a Jew. When we came back under the Persians and the Medes, a man who could not show from his father's house who he came from was given no inheritance, and a Levite could not serve in his office. Zerubbabel could show he came from King David's line.

The daughters of Zelophehad show the law when a man has only daughters. They asked, “Why should the name of our father be done away from among his family, because he hath no son?” The Lord said, “If a man die, and have no son, then ye shall cause his inheritance to pass unto his daughter”, then to his brother, then his father's brethren, then the next kinsman: the law Boaz was fulfilling. But those daughters had to marry “only to the family of the tribe of their father”, “So shall not the inheritance of the children of Israel remove from tribe to tribe.” The inheritance of Israel is paternal. There is no sin in marrying a woman of another tribe; Aaron did it. The command there was only to keep the land in the tribe. We have no land in captivity now, so marry within your nation and stay with your people.

precepts.label: 1 Chronicles 28:19
precepts.why:
David, chosen out of Judah and out of his father’s house, hands the building of the house to the son the Lord chose to sit on the throne: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.” “Moreover I will establish his kingdom for ever”. Solomon’s kingdom, not Solomon and his brethren’s. Then David charges him: “Take heed now; for the Lord hath chosen thee to build an house for the sanctuary: be strong, and do it.”

“Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch”. The blueprints to the temple: guess who gave them to Solomon? David. Solomon did not come up with the design; David came up with it, and Solomon fulfilled his father’s wishes. That porch is why the feast of dedication is kept at Solomon’s porch. It took Solomon seven years to build the temple and thirteen years to build his own house, so the temple was done before his house was finished.

David gave him the pattern “of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper chambers thereof”, the floors and levels, “and of the inner parlours thereof, and of the place of the mercy seat”, the holy of holies. “And the pattern of all that he had by the spirit”: the spirit moved David to design the temple. The courses of the priests, which priest for burning incense and which for each service, David was behind all of that too. Gold by weight for the things of gold, “refined gold by weight” for the altar of incense, everything gold, “and gold for the pattern of the chariot of the cherubims, that spread out their wings, and covered the ark of the covenant of the Lord.”

“All this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing by his hand upon me, even all the works of this pattern.” David did not write it off the top of his head. The Lord moved his hand on what to write, and David drew out the temple through his hands. So the house Solomon built on the throne of the kingdom of the Lord was the Lord’s own pattern, given through David to the son chosen to sit on David’s throne.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:47
precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. The Lord gave us the abundance of all things, and we did not want to serve him for it. So he caused us to serve our enemies, and that is why we ended up falling underneath these people. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

Before we went into captivity we were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. Psalms 96:5 is his message and warning to us: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” Our God made everything; that is the God we are connected with. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

We are not the nations. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” “He hath not dealt so with any nation”. Our customs are his statutes and judgments; we have the Bible, not idols. And Jeremiah 10 says, “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”, “Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” Astrology, witchcraft and voodoo are the nations' problem, not ours. The Israelites are a special people, set above the nations, the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:12-13
precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction”. Where does pride begin? Sirach: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: the beginning of you falling to sin, falling for your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite. You knew better. You had all the warning signs, all the opportunity, everything placed in front of you. You were given a way out, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 said: God will with the temptation make a way to escape. But pride overcame you. Your mind wasn't on the Lord when your back was against the wall.

“and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”. When you have that pride, a negro is unstoppable; a prideful negro, oh my God. “and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds things to your demise: I'm going to leave you to Satan to gobble you on up, because your mind ain't right; you're too prideful.

That is why pride goes before destruction. Pride removes correction; you don't want to hear it. You think you know it all, you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride isolates you, and it precedes the collapse.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:3
precepts.why:
Sirach says pride begins when one departs from God. The Wisdom of Solomon shows how a man departs: “For froward thoughts separate from God”.

Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible. Period. That's what it is.

When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him. You can't be both. So pride starts in the thoughts: the moment your thinking goes outside of the scriptures, you have separated yourself from God, and a haughty spirit is on its way to the fall. That is why the man who meditates on the scriptures has something to pull from when temptation comes, and the froward man doesn't.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 25:1-2
precepts.why:
This is how much the Lord hates pride. Sirach first shows what God loves: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren the Lord loves; the love of neighbors the Lord loves. And a man and wife that agree together: why is that beautiful? Because it's hard for two different personalities to come together and be on the same accord. That's why marriage takes time, brothers and sisters. It isn't overnight; it takes years and experience.

Now the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.” He is offended at their life. A negro that's poor and proud: I hate that negro, I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. How can you be that way?

It means you have no humility whatsoever. Nobody can tell you anything; you have all the answers, but no fruits in your life, no solutions, no shame. That is the pride that goes before destruction, and God's soul hates it.

Notice we start first with setting our own houses in order; then we have the ability to tell somebody else to get right and fix their stuff.

If we are going to set our houses in order, where do we start? With your marriage; that is the first place. If the home front isn't right, how are you going to get out there and instruct your people? There is one word that is often wanted but is hurtful to say, so God says it. Your scum is still in your mouth, sisters.

Scum is a layer of foul or unwanted matter that forms on top of a liquid, such as pond scum or soap scum. Informally it means a despised, immoral or worthless person or group, the scum of the earth. The slang meaning goes further: the epitome of a worthless, good-for-nothing human, at the bottom of the hierarchy of humans, possibly the worst word you can have your name associated with. It describes someone so disgraceful they are seen as the lowest form of life: worthlessness, a waste of skin, dirt, nothing. Because it is perfectly acceptable English and not a swear, it is even more demeaning; it is used only when it is the only word for the job, and it makes the victim feel like the lowest of the low.

That is the word God chose for his own people when she wore herself out with lies and the wickedness would not come out of her. Some of these evil sisters are the scum of the earth; that is what God is saying. So examine yourself, and open your mouth with wisdom and the law of kindness instead.

precepts.label: Sirach 25:26
precepts.why:
“whoso pleaseth God shall escape from her; but the sinner shall be taken by her.” A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man. But what about the man who complains of a wicked woman and claims he is not wicked himself? If that is true, he will find a way to escape. Sirach shows the way: “If she go not as thou wouldest have her, cut her off from thy flesh, and give her a bill of divorce, and let her go.”

This is the brother in the world trying to repent, trying to get his house in order and straighten it out, while his wife keeps up the traps of Ecclesiastes 7:26: her heart snares and nets, her hands as bands, creating chaos and assignments so he can't get to camp, to the brothers, to the meetings. She doesn't want to listen. Then let her go. And it goes both ways; it is about you men too.

But understand: this is not talking about a biblical marriage. Once you get married in this truth, she is yours for life, unless she commits adultery. There is no divorce in the Bible, and we don't dissolve marriages up in here; it is written in our rules. This is for those coming in from outside this truth, with all kinds of situations.

So the man who pleases God escapes from her. But if you allow yourself to be destroyed, you were indeed wicked, and the woman sent to you was your portion for real.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:15
precepts.why:
Paul speaks to the same case: “But if the unbelieving depart, let him depart. A brother or a sister is not under bondage in such cases: but God hath called us to peace.”

The man was wicked and inherited a wicked woman. Why? God orchestrated it, to see whether he would stay there, and to reflect what is in us so that we can change. The Lord is interested in the elect, so he puts us through trials and temptations to see if we will overcome them.

The bondage is the worldly marriage. When the spouse says, I don't care what you do, I want nothing to do with that Bible, and makes it plain and won't bend, still cooking pork and ham hocks on one side of the stove, this half is for you since you're keeping those laws, we're going to keep eating chitlins and hog maws, the house smelling like butt: if the unbelieving depart, let them depart. That is the woman of Ecclesiastes 7:26 whose heart is traps and nets, and whoso pleases God shall escape.

But those coming out of these situations have a lot of work to do before they can even think about properly marrying, and brothers and sisters are impatient. Leadership are the fathers of the men and women, and we have the records. When we tell you to lean back and let the brother or sister work on themselves, it is for a good reason, because the backdoor marriage stories are horrible, and they get worse every time a new one pops up.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:1-4
precepts.why:
Before anyone walks away, look at the other side. At a Passover panel years ago a sister asked when she could walk away from her husband in the world. They had been together about ten years, through Africanism, through Islam, through different things. In his mind this truth might be just another fad. Wait, sister. Lean back.

“Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.” He is worldly, but he isn't telling you to break the laws of God, so still deal with him properly. Chaste means with discipline: you aren't cursing him out. He watches the change in you, sees the fear of the Lord in you, and sees it is serious, not a phase.

“Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel; But let it be the hidden man of the heart”, “the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.” She puts on proper clothing, and tells him: my husband, I want you to come in and take command, so I can deal with you as a proper wife. He comes home from catching hell at work and she knows how to pull him out of it, and he asks, where are you learning this wisdom? If he is righteous, he comes in behind you; we have seen it many times.

Men do the same: a brother who was in sin with his wife last week wants to turn the house upside down this week. Give her a chance to see you're serious. Wives have said, I didn't know he was this serious; he was willing to let me go, and they came in behind him. That is the Most High giving righteousness to righteousness.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Man was put on this earth to rule it with God's commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering; we are not in power. The earth was made to receive your direction, men.

Paul shows it: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Expectation means I am expecting something, and earnestly means with a begging type of attitude. The creation is earnestly waiting for the manifestation, and manifestation means the growth: time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men, to get ourselves together. The earth is waiting for the sons of God to manifest into gods, that is, to rule this planet properly.

And righteous women are waiting for that too. The woman is called woman because she is of man, and she is like the earth: you plant your seed in her and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. She is supposed to revolve around you, and when you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction. That is why women cry, where are our black men? The father figure in the house got destroyed.

All of it fell apart when we broke the laws of the Most High from the very beginning, when the woman was out of order with her husband. So it is up to us men to fulfil the duty of manhood to fix it: to marry, build a nation, and rule rightly. That is what the whole creation is waiting on.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:14
precepts.why:
Verse 13 gives the whole duty of man; verse 14 gives the reason: “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” For means because. Keep his commandments, because this is the whole reason God put man on the earth, and because God shall bring every work into judgment.

So if we are not dealing with our marriages properly, there is going to be a judgment for that, and we are looking at it. People try to figure out the problem in the black community: the marriages are messed up. Whoring, adultery, fornication. A little leaven will destroy the whole congregation, and it has to be rooted out like a cancer.

“with every secret thing”: the nasty stuff people do behind closed doors, thinking nobody sees. In nearly 35 years in this truth, we have seen the Most High bring out what people thought they could hide, and he brings it out at the worst time for you. Like applying for a job years later, thinking you got away with it, and they pull records you didn't know existed: get out of my office. That's how the Lord is.

So keep your slate clean. Be a disciplined man: you may not always be motivated, but you must always be disciplined. When sin comes before you, it stops right there. Because every work, good or evil, is going to come out, we have to be men of holiness, integrity, righteousness, dignity, honor and valor. That is the whole duty of man.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 10:20
precepts.why:
God shall bring every secret thing into judgment, and the Lord even calls a bird to bring it out: “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.” We have sat in judgments where they asked, how did he find out? It's that damn bird. Somebody might think it's a literal bird flying around; I took every precaution. But the Most High is going to bring it out anyway. That's why it says every secret thing.

No, not in thy thought. Some people speak against the council and the leadership, or have evil thoughts against the leaders, and think they will get away with it. The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The goal is to give a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to counsel and got herself together. When they will not take counsel, the leader still has to give an account, with grief.

This is how we should have grown up. We grew up in a lawless society; in slavery the fathers were stripped from the homes and the men forced to give their seed but not allowed to raise it. The matter will be told on you in your evil, so fear God, keep his commandments, and honor the ones set over you.

precepts.label: Isaiah 8:18
precepts.why:
Isaiah had just told Ahaz, “the Lord himself shall give you a sign”. Then in chapter 8 the Lord has Isaiah write the name Maher-shalal-hash-baz, quick to the plunder, swift to the spoil, and Isaiah goes unto the prophetess, his wife, and “she conceived, and bare a son.” The child was named before he was conceived, the same way Gabriel named John and named Christ before they were conceived.

Then Isaiah says who the sign is: “Behold, I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs and for wonders in Israel from the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth in mount Zion.” Behold who? I, Isaiah, and the children. Not his wife. He never counts the woman.

So the sign of Isaiah 7:14 was not the virgin; it was the child. The virgin birth was garbage. The birth of Isaiah's son was the sign that Ephraim and Syria banding together against Judah would fail. Before the child could cry “My father, and my mother,” the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria were taken away before the king of Assyria. Assyria would pass through Judah and “reach even to the neck”, coming close to conquering but failing, because of Immanuel: “Take counsel together, and it shall come to nought; speak the word, and it shall not stand: for God is with us.” Once Isaiah's son was born, the two kings could not succeed against Judah.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 12:6
precepts.why:
The Lord told Ezekiel to bear his stuff on his shoulders in their sight and carry it forth in the twilight, covering his face “that thou see not the ground: for I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel.” God made Ezekiel himself a sign unto the house of Israel.

Read on to verse 11 and Ezekiel is told to say it to Israel plainly: “Say, I am your sign: like as I have done, so shall it be done unto them: they shall remove and go into captivity.” What the prophet did, Israel would go through.

This lines up with Isaiah 8. When the Lord gives a sign, it is the man and the child he gives, not the woman. Isaiah and his children were signs and wonders in Israel, and Ezekiel was set for a sign to the house of Israel, which is why the sign of Isaiah 7:14 is the child born to Isaiah and the prophetess.

precepts.label: Ezekiel 24:24
precepts.why:
“Thus Ezekiel is unto you a sign.” What is he? A sign. Not his wife: Ezekiel. “according to all that he hath done shall ye do: and when this cometh, ye shall know that I am the Lord God.”

The Lord told Ezekiel to eat dung, and what did we end up doing? Eating dung. He was a sign, and what he did came upon Israel.

Read on to verse 27: “thou shalt be a sign unto them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.” Again and again the man is the sign. So when Isaiah says “I and the children whom the Lord hath given me are for signs”, it fits the pattern of the prophets: the sign given to Ahaz was the child Isaiah's wife bare, Maher-shalal-hash-baz, not a virgin.

precepts.label: Luke 11:29-30
precepts.why:
When the people were gathered thick together, Christ said, “This is an evil generation: they seek a sign; and there shall no sign be given it, but the sign of Jonas the prophet.” Then: “For as Jonas was a sign unto the Ninevites, so shall also the Son of man be to this generation.”

Jonas was a sign. The Son of man was a sign. Men were always the signs. There is no scripture where the women were signs. Hosea was also a sign, and his marriage was a sign, but the woman by herself was never a sign.

That settles Isaiah 7 and 8. The Lord said he would give Ahaz a sign, and Isaiah tells us who it was: himself and the children the Lord gave him. The son born to Isaiah and the prophetess was the sign that God was with Judah, Immanuel, and that the two kings coming against Judah would come to nought.

precepts.label: Genesis 29:22-23
precepts.why:
Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

So Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. He came into this world as a son of man, made flesh and blood like his brethren, and that is how he fulfils the promise to David.

precepts.label: Ruth 4:13
precepts.why:
Gabriel tells Mary, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”. It is the same word used of her cousin: “And after those days his wife Elisabeth conceived”. What does it mean to conceive? To conceive you need seed; the man’s seed has to go in and fertilize the egg. Some might be confused, so Ruth shows how that happens.

“So Boaz took Ruth, and she was his wife: and when he went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception, and she bare a son.” When Boaz went in unto her, the Lord gave her conception. That is how it works: a husband goes in unto his wife, and the Lord gives the conception.

And when Luke 1:28 says the angel “came in unto her”, he came in and talked with her. He did not come in and have sex with her; he came in and talked to her, plain and simple. So when Luke 1:31 says Mary shall conceive, it is conception the way Ruth conceived, the Lord giving it when her husband came unto her. It could well have been the first time Joseph touched her that the Lord made her conceive.

precepts.label: Leviticus 12:2
precepts.why:
The law shows what conceiving is: “Speak unto the children of Israel, saying, If a woman have conceived seed, and born a man child: then she shall be unclean seven days”. She conceived what? Seed.

A woman conceives seed through intercourse. That is the same seed Onan spilled on the ground in Genesis 38, knowing the inheritance would not be his. It is the same exact thing.

So Luke 1:31, “thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son”, is a woman conceiving seed and bearing a man child. It is said to Mary in the same form of words as to Zacharias about Elisabeth: “thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John,” and “shalt call his name JESUS.” The same thing being done, the same thing being said.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 19:7-8
precepts.why:
Luke 1:35 says “the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee”. What does overshadow mean? Wisdom of Solomon shows it: “For the whole creature in his proper kind was fashioned again anew, serving the peculiar commandments that were given unto them, that thy children might be kept without hurt”. The whole creature is Israel, the whole nation that came out of Egypt, made new, serving the peculiar commandments.

“As namely, a cloud shadowing the camp; and where water stood before, dry land appeared; and out of the Red sea a way without impediment; and out of the violent stream a green field: Wherethrough all the people went that were defended with thy hand, seeing thy marvellous strange wonders.”

What did the cloud shadowing the camp do for us at the Red Sea? It led us. It guided us through the Red Sea, and the people went through “defended with thy hand.” That is what overshadow means: to lead, guide and defend.

So when the angel says the power of the Highest shall overshadow Mary, it is not the spirit coming into her and making her pregnant. It is the Lord guiding and defending her, leading her to where she had to go.

precepts.label: Baruch 5:7-9
precepts.why:
Baruch gives another one. Overshadow does not mean that it got her impregnated. It means to guide her to where she had to go. “For God hath appointed that every high hill, and banks of long continuance, should be cast down, and valleys filled up, to make even the ground, that Israel may go safely in the glory of God”.

“Moreover even the woods and every sweetsmelling tree shall overshadow Israel by the commandment of God. For God shall lead Israel with joy in the light of his glory”. The trees shall overshadow Israel, for God shall lead Israel. To overshadow is to lead, guide or defend.

So in Luke 1:35 the Lord would lead Mary to Joseph. When it says overshadow thee, it means he will guide and lead her, like he led Zacharias home to his wife to lay with her. That is what it is talking about, not him overshadowing her into pregnancy.

precepts.label: Proverbs 20:24
precepts.why:
This goes with overshadow: the Lord guided Mary, and she went and came together with her husband. “Man’s goings are of the Lord; how can a man then understand his own way?”

A man’s goings are of the Lord because the Lord guides us and overshadows us in everyday life. Sometimes you are walking in the street, something tells you to pick something up off the ground, and a car goes right by where you would have been. Why? The Lord was there guiding you.

“how can a man then understand his own way?” Remember, Mary did not understand. She said, “How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?” She was espoused to Joseph but had not yet come together with him. The Lord said, don’t worry, you are going to fulfil the scriptures; I am going to guide you. She could not understand her way, but the Most High had plans for her, and he guided her, the same way he guided every one of us here.
