precepts.label: Genesis 1:2
precepts.why:
The kingdom of heaven is the nation of Israel. That is why the apostles asked in Acts whether Christ would at that time restore the kingdom to Israel, and why the Pharisees asked when it would come. “The kingdom of God cometh not with observation”. We look for it to come from somewhere outside. We externalize everything instead of taking up what is already in us. The Lord put a mind and a spirit in us to build and to organize.

You were made after the image of your Father, and Genesis shows how he created. “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was without form and void”. The earth did not yet exist physically, but it existed in God's mind. If he calls it earth, it existed; it existed in his mind. It was void in physical existence. “and darkness was upon the face of the deep”: the deep is the elements God used to fashion the earth. He manipulated the elements to materialize what was pictured in his mind. “And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters”: the Spirit moved upon the elements.

“And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” God imagined what light should be. “And God saw the light, that it was good”: when he created it, he compared it to the image in his mind, and it was good, meaning it conformed to his thoughts. He did the same with the earth: when it was all done he said it is good, because it matched the earth he had in mind before it was even created.

Because we are made in his image, we have the ability to do the same thing: to organize and put things together in our minds before they become physical. That is what Christ is saying: “Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.” Everything you lay your eyes on, apart from the ground, the vegetation and the water, came from a thought. People cannot believe that IUIC can envision its buildings before bringing them into existence, but we are supposed to think like our Father. If filthy thoughts can become filthy words, actions, character and destiny, the same mind can materialize righteousness and build the city on the hill that is already in your mind.

“the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.” The Romans took the kingdom away from us by force. Part of the kingdom of heaven is being able to envision our nation and lay down the foundations for how it should operate, here on this earth, with our children, our women, everyone in order. Christ and the angels will come and give it to us physically, with power, but our minds have to be ready for it, so we need to be rehearsing it now.

precepts.label: Matthew 23:32
precepts.why:
The disciples asked, “Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?” They were asking about something Christ had taught them, the regeneration. How could the man have sinned to be paying for it with blindness from birth, unless he was here before? Christ did not say, what are you talking about. He answered that in this case it was neither, “but that the works of God should be made manifest in him”.

But paying for the sins of the fathers is real, and Matthew 23 shows how it works. Christ tells the scribes and Pharisees, “ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity”. They “build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets”. They were saying, that wasn't us.

Christ answers: “Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers”. They came back generations later proclaiming to be righteous, but they were the ones doing the killing back then. Fill ye up means reap what you sow: it's time to pay for what you did.

It works the same way for the nations and for us. Those who led us into captivity on the slave ships have not yet gone into captivity, but they are going, because they have to fill up the measure of their fathers. And we had to fill up the measure of ours: the same spirits Moses stood in front of at Sinai and told they would go back to Egypt in ships came back generations later and went on those ships.

precepts.label: Exodus 34:7
precepts.why:
Exodus 34:7 makes it super clear. The Lord is “Keeping mercy for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and that will by no means clear the guilty”. The guilty were those that killed the prophets. He is “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation”.

The iniquity of the fathers was the murder of the prophets, and it was visited upon the children, the Pharisees of Christ's day. That is what Christ meant by “Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers”: you were your fathers, doing the killing back then. Those born in the third and fourth generation pay for the sins committed three or four generations ago.

So the man born blind in John 9 was not paying for his own sin. The Most High caused him to be born blind so that he could be healed later, and the Lord may allow a situation anywhere so he can exercise his mercy and his power on it as an example to the rest of us. People needed to see that Christ could heal. The Lord has people's lives plotted out for what he needs them to be.

But that is not an excuse to do evil. Don't be so confident in his mercy that you go out and play with the Most High's judgment, because he will by no means clear the guilty, and you might not even make it in here.

But it is not going to be returned unless the man is in his proper order. The Most High is not going to give the kingdom to the women and not the men; there is no glory for the sisters unless the men get their glory as prophesied.

Some sisters make a face at that and say, I love Jesus directly. So Paul backs it up: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” It is the same thing: there is no salvation except through Christ, and the man is the saviour of the body. The flock of the pasture is men, and the saviours on Mount Zion are men.

Look at the so-called white woman, whom the other women worship, with the Vogue magazines and Miss America. She would have none of that if she did not support her man; the man had to guarantee her sovereignty and her safety so she could prance around. Those women were behind their men a thousand percent, even in evil, going out to the lynchings to support them. Yet that same man keeps his woman in check and tells our women they don't need you brothers. All women expect their men to guarantee their protection; the fact that this must even be addressed among our women is evidence of our destruction.

The charger only has a need because the phone was created. The woman is the charging station, but with no phone you aren't charging nothing. The charger came out of the phone: woman was taken out of man, and she is a helpmate and a comfort to him so he can guarantee her protection and the offspring. You won't get past this brother, because you came from the brother. So the charging stations need to be in full force, and the men have to get in order so the kingdom can be restored.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 14:2
precepts.why:
When Paul was led into the castle, the chief captain asked, “Canst thou speak Greek? Art not thou that Egyptian, which before these days madest an uproar, and leddest out into the wilderness four thousand men that were murderers?” He took Paul for a specific Egyptian. “But Paul said, I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Paul passed for an Egyptian. Moses passed for an Egyptian. Joseph passed for an Egyptian. Christ passed too: his family ran into Africa from white folks. What more do you possibly need at this point?

Jeremiah shows what Judah looked like: “Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up.” Jeremiah is speaking of the same situation he wrote of in Lamentations, when Babylon came, overthrew us and starved us. We became blacker to the ground: dark, swelled bellies, ribs showing, ribs touching. That is how we looked when Babylon besieged us for those years.

Some try to say it is only symbolic. No: it is the same thing, and Jeremiah, who wrote Lamentations, is saying the same thing in both places. Calling it symbolic is simple and unfaithful and weak.

So the chief captain looking at a Jew and seeing an Egyptian makes sense. Judah was black, and a Jew of Tarsus could pass for an Egyptian because our people looked like the people of Africa. Israel sits in Western Asia bordering North Africa, one land mass, and all the native inhabitants of that region were nonwhite.

precepts.label: 2 Chronicles 31:21
precepts.why:
“Where is boasting then? It is excluded. By what law? of works? Nay: but by the law of faith.” What are the works Paul is talking about? Not what your son did today while you were at work. One so-called leader stood up and asked a room if you go home and ask your son what his deeds were today. Who does that? He is an idiot, and whoever listens to him needs to repent.

Chronicles shows what the works are: “And in every work that he began in the service of the house of God, and in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.” The works are the works done in the service of the house of God: the sacrificial law.

Earlier in the same chapter, “Hezekiah appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites after their courses, every man according to his service, the priests and Levites for burnt offerings and for peace offerings”. Those are the works of God in the temple.

So when Paul says boasting is excluded, it means you cannot boast that you are sacrificing, as though it makes you something special, because that is done: Christ died for us. The justification is through Christ, by faith, not by the works of the temple service.

precepts.label: Nehemiah 13:11-14
precepts.why:
“Therefore we conclude that a man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.” What are the deeds of the law? Nehemiah shows them: “Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.” We are talking about the house of God.

“Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.” This is what they brought: the offerings. He “made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah”, “for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.”

“Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.” The deeds were the sacrifices and offerings he brought to the house of God.

And it is in the same chapter of Romans where God is justified in his sayings and overcomes when he is judged: let God be true, and every man a liar. This is serious. Your salvation is at hand, and a teacher who is up at the podium drinking, talking about sex and baby oil and prostitution, instead of instructing the people what these scriptures are talking about, is not a leader to lead people to God. He is a joke.

precepts.label: Sirach 44:4
precepts.why:
How do you identify a leader? Some people say you can’t say he’s not a leader. Yes, we can, because you can tell who a man is by his speech. Sirach gives the rubric: “Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions”.

Leaders of the people by their counsels: you should be able to tell by their godly counsel, coming from the Bible, whether or not they are leaders of the people. By their knowledge of learning meet for the people: Bishop just showed the works in Chronicles and the deeds in Nehemiah 13, proving what Romans 3 means. Wise and eloquent are their instructions.

The leaders here in Israel United in Christ prove everything they say with the scriptures. That is why I am here. Why are you there? What is your agenda? Are you there because he talks about baby oil? Are you there because he cannot break down Romans 3? The Bible is the rubric that lets us know who the real leaders are and who are not.

precepts.label: 2 Timothy 2:15-16
precepts.why:

The brother who said a man’s deeds are what his son did today embarrassed the hell out of himself and his organization. Now he is being clowned, and because he represents the Israelite community, they label us all as stupid. And never trust a man wearing dark sunglasses inside: he can hide his embarrassment and his eyes. Brother, you have to repent and change your ways.

“But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness.” That is profane and vain babbling; it doesn’t make any sense. And nobody in the room, nobody equal to his rank, says, hey, listen, brother, next time. He keeps having a pattern of doing the same thing.

Here, if a captain starts talking crazy, a captain junior to him is going to correct him, because we represent Israel United in Christ, and our elders have taught us with knowledge, wisdom and understanding how to conduct ourselves. There are checks and balances. That brother does not have any of that, and so he cannot rightly divide Romans 3.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 5:42
precepts.why:
Solomon said, “The thing that hath been, it is that which shall be; and that which is done is that which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.” Paul says the same thing in different words: “For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning”. Our learning today. There are no new incidents on this earth; everything that was done in the past is reoccurring.

Ezra shows it with a ring: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”. A ring is like a circle. “like as there is no slackness of the last, even so there is no swiftness of the first”. Slackness means slow: there is no slowness of the last judgments and no swiftness of the first. His judgments on the earth are a continual event that reoccurs over and over; it is the same thing.

That is why Paul said to comfort ourselves through what is written in the testimonies of the past: what we are living is a reoccurring event. To deal with these reoccurring events we must read the history and testimonies of our ancestors, “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.”

We see it now. Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden image and gathered the rulers to its dedication, setting up a one world religion; today pastors gather to pray over and dedicate a towering gold statue of Donald Trump. What we read in Daniel 3 is coming to pass again, because the judgments go around like a ring.

precepts.label: Hosea 12:10
precepts.why:
The things written aforetime were written for our learning, and Hosea shows how they were written: “I have also spoken by the prophets, and I have multiplied visions, and used similitudes, by the ministry of the prophets.”

All the prophets spoke: Isaiah, Jeremiah, Daniel, even Hosea. God multiplied visions, and he used similitudes, or parables, by the ministry of the prophets, comparing one thing to another.

That is how the scriptures teach us today. The past is a similitude of what is happening now, and by comparing one thing to another we can see our own time in what was written. The last beast of Revelation 13 is described with the leopard, the bear and the lion of Daniel 7: it carries the attributes of Greece, Persia and Media, and Babylon. The golden image of Daniel 3 stands again in our day.

So we read the prophets as similitudes, and through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, because the Most High already showed in the past what he will do in the future.

precepts.label: Psalms 136:8-17
precepts.why:
Paul says God “will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape”. There is no temptation that should derail us from inheriting the wide place, the kingdom that sits within the narrow passage (2 Esdras 7), because God's mercies endure for ever. David shows that mercy: “The sun to rule by day: for his mercy endureth for ever: The moon and stars to rule by night: for his mercy endureth for ever.” The Lord declared the end from the beginning and created all of this. We acknowledge his greatness and his mercy, and we tap into that comfort under the shadow of his wings.

“To him that smote Egypt in their firstborn: for his mercy endureth for ever: And brought out Israel from among them”. The Most High killed our enemies for us because he had mercy on us. We cried in Egypt, the Lord heard our cries and said, go down, Moses, tell Pharaoh to let my people go, or I will kill his firstborn.

“With a strong hand, and with a stretched out arm”, “To him which divided the Red sea into parts”, “And made Israel to pass through the midst of it”, “But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red sea”, “To him which led his people through the wilderness”, “To him which smote great kings: for his mercy endureth for ever”.

We saw all of this, and we still get here today and do evil, just as our fathers under the cloud did. The Most High is trying to set us back up, but he wants to make sure we are in the right spiritual posture to inherit the kingdom. He lets us use his Bible as spiritual weapons to fight off the evil temptations so we can get to the wide.

precepts.label: Lamentations 3:20-24
precepts.why:
Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

precepts.label: Psalms 23:5
precepts.why:
God will with the temptation “make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” While we endure the encounters of temptation that are common to us all, even the temptations of our own lusts, the Lord prepares a table for us: “Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.” Why? Because his mercies endure for ever.

The table is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables”. Isaiah shows it: “write it before them in a table, and note it in a book”. The tables are what we are supposed to be reading.

But we read the tables and talk about what's going on overseas while our own spirit is rotten. We read it like entertainment instead of changing what is really going on in us.

Brothers and sisters, you are in the greatest place on the planet earth, and some of you don't even realize it. You are getting teaching that tells you what is happening in the future, because we know the future from reading the Bible. And some of you play games, scorn what is brought out, and take this for a joke. The table is prepared in the presence of our enemies; eat from it.

precepts.label: Habakkuk 2:2
precepts.why:
The table the Lord prepares before us in the presence of our enemies is the Bible. Habakkuk shows it: “And the Lord answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.”

The Lord told the prophet Habakkuk: since you want to get out of captivity, write the vision down, and make it plain upon the tables. That is what we are supposed to be reading.

Make it plain “that he may run that readeth it”: when we bring this out, everybody is going to be running, and we are going to run to teach it. The Bible is going to turn this whole system upside down: these are they which have turned the world upside down. But we have to be in it like that, not reading about overseas like entertainment while our own spirit is rotten.

precepts.label: Isaiah 30:8
precepts.why:
Paul says what happened to our fathers is “written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” Isaiah shows why it was written: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”.

This is to the wicked Israelites, us, our people. Go write it before them in a table, and put a note in the book about their wickedness, our wickedness, “that it may be for the time to come”: for today.

And it goes on: “That this is a rebellious people”. That is what is going on with our people; our people are rebellious. But the Bible is here to correct you and straighten you out. If you want it, there is a way for you to get it.

Those who refuse to learn from the past by reading it are doomed to repeat it. You will repeat it because you refuse to learn, and the same spirits will follow you and attach themselves to you, the way people move to a new town, a new job or a new congregation and the same problem follows. The Lord sends those spirits as a mirror to show you what is wrong in you. Learn it from the book, and you won't have to learn it again.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 14:20-21
precepts.why:
“There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. The Lord still gives you enough strength not to be overtaken, and always a way out. But it is up to you. Sometimes we are weak in the faith and weak in the spirit: you don't read your four chapters a day, your conversation is not about the scriptures, you are not around the brothers, and Satan gets a hold of you.

When we do not study, we have nothing in our spirits to combat Satan; we are defenseless. Even Christ, when he was tempted, used the word of God: as it is written. We have to be the same way. Sirach: “Blessed is the man that doth meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.”

When you meditate on good things, you can reason in the scriptures in the moment of temptation: wait, the scripture says this; I can't do that. “He that considereth her ways in his heart” is always asking, what does the scripture say about this? That is how you combat the lust, the demon: you have to have something in your spirit.

When you go before the magistrates you are told not to think about what you will say, but you still have to have something in your spirit for the Lord to work with. If you have no scriptures about lust in your head, where are you going to pull from? Give the Holy Spirit something to work with. When Joseph, our forefather in Egypt, was tempted, he went straight back to the law: I would be sinning against God. That came to his mind first because his mind was always on the scriptures. Temptation always comes with an exit; addiction forms when we stop taking the exit.

precepts.label: John 5:30
precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Is anybody confused on the order? Then why are there so many problems in Israel, so much confusion about the husband's position and the wife's position? Because pride has made its way in, and confusion has set itself in the house.

“and the head of Christ is God”. Was Christ ever confused, at any moment in his life, about his position and role with the Father? He said: “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.”

Christ said, I am doing exactly as the Father told me to do. Is he doing what he wants? No. Christ understands his role and his position. And Christ now tells us the husband is the head of the wife. So why is there still so much confusion? Somebody does not believe like they say they do.

It happens on both sides of the room. Brother, because of your lack of leadership, because you are non-confrontational and passive and don't want no smoke, she raises her voice and you cower; she walks by shoulder-bumping you, and you can't raise your voice in your own house. All because you gave up your position. Some brothers want to be mama's boys: you didn't want a wife, you wanted a mom. If Christ submits to the head over him, the husband must take his place under Christ, and the wife her place under her husband.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:23
precepts.why:
“But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.” Paul is not making anything up. He is not creating a list and saying, I'll place this person here and that person there. He went to the divine order that was set forth from the beginning, when Adam named his wife Eve, and he does it in other places too.

Ephesians says it again: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church”. Is there any confusion there, brothers? The husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church.

So the order runs: the Most High God, Christ, the husband, and the wife. If anybody tries to step out of their role or out of their position, what are they? The damn devil. That goes for the men too: men who step out of their role and want to be a mama's boy, you are the damn devil. You have been given a position; you must fill it.

There cannot be a commandment you are negotiating on. All of us struggle with something, and we know the fight, but never be the one who says, I can get with everything else but that right there I just can't do; he's an idiot, I can't follow him. That is not what the scripture said.

precepts.label: Colossians 1:18
precepts.why:
“the head of every man is Christ”. Colossians shows it: “And he is the head of the body, the church: who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead”. Christ is the head of the church.

And Christ himself is under a head: “the head of Christ is God.” Christ said, “The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do”. And, “the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth”. How could the Father show the Son if the Son was the Father? If you are still stuck on the Trinity, go sit in the corner. It makes no sense for the Most High to show his Son something if they are the same entity.

“For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son”. Here we see order being given, and the headship of the household falls under the same order. “That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father.” To honour the Son is to honour what he said; if you do not honour the order God has given you, you are not honouring the Lord.

Christ said, “I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me.” He is letting us know that he himself is in the divine order and submits to the position he has been given. What do we look like doing anything other than what Christ did?

precepts.label: 2 Corinthians 11:2
precepts.why:
“For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband”. The espousal was made when the Most High sent his son Christ, because Christ died for us, his woman. We are the woman of the Most High. We are men physically, but we are his bride, and that is why Paul uses that term.

He cleaned us up. Sanctified them through thy truth; thy word is truth. Once he cleaned us up, we became virgins with him: “that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” That is crystal clear. It is what 2 Corinthians 5:17 means: “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away”.

There is such a thing as history, but your history only comes up if you keep doing what you used to do. Then it becomes a blot on your record today. None of us was born in this truth, so whatever you sisters went through, and the same with you brothers, clean yourselves up while you are here. All of us have a chance to get ourselves correct.

Once the slate is cleaned, we do not dirty it up. We do not defile it or mess it up. That is how we stay a chaste virgin espoused to Christ.

precepts.label: Revelation 14:4
precepts.why:
“These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” That does not necessarily mean they are virgins physically. They are virgins in this truth. They put off the weak nature, the sins and the cares of the world. They are the ones that came in and repented, the new creature of 2 Corinthians 5:17, where old things are passed away and all things are become new.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men”: redeemed from among the filth. To be redeemed means you were in the filth, in the vomit, at a serious deficit, and you had to be brought up out of it. We were redeemed from that, “being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” We have been cleaned up for the Lord, men and women, so we have a chance and an opportunity to get it right.

“And in their mouth was found no guile”: no lies, “for they are without fault before the throne of God.” How can that be? Only when you are keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Christ.

So watch how you move. Replay your own actions in your mind, see how you are operating, and catch yourself, because there is an effort to take us off our path. The virgins who follow the Lamb keep the slate clean.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 6:17
thread.text: Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,

classes.title: Transforming From Immorality To Beautiful Civility Returning Our Kingdom To An Organized Nation Pt 3

precepts.label: 1 Peter 5:5
precepts.why:
“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. When the brothers teach on the street, that is what they tell our brothers and sisters: come out of the sinful lives you are living in, out of Babylon the great, out of these wicked holidays like Christmas. But if we tell them to come out of something, they have to come into something. They have to have something to say yes to, like righteously enjoying the commandments of the Lord through the high holy days. An organized nation thinks on all of these points and deals with the nation holistically.

They lose their wicked parents and wicked friends when they come in, so the Lord says “I will receive you”, and “will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters”. Your fathers out there did not teach you anything. Your mothers did not teach you anything. So the Lord gives you fathers and mothers in this truth.

That is why Peter says “Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder.” When our brothers and sisters come in, they are going to have to submit to the leadership, to the elders who now stand as their fathers and mothers.

When you are received, you are not abandoned or left out in the cold. You were lost, but now you are found: welcome home. Now we have belonging, now we are loved, wrapped in the Most High's care, and that makes you stand up with esteem and refuse to let mediocrity deter you from the righteous path.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 5:2
precepts.why:
“The elder women as mothers”. The mothers out there did not teach anything. The daughters ran wild, the sons ran wild, and the daddies taught nothing. But the children heard the prophets say, come out of that. So the elder women in this truth become mothers to the sisters who come in without proper guidance. That is the importance of you elders, and why we thank the Lord for the sisters still holding on to righteousness, because Satan went after our sisters and got a lot of them messed up.

“the younger as sisters”: the younger women become sisters to the disenfranchised sisters coming in. A sister who comes in does not know how to put a skirt on, dress properly, carry herself or hold a righteous conversation. She learns from sisters who were guided by proper mothers and fathers in the body. The brothers are the same: we are a proper influence on brothers who came from total dysfunction. And it is to be done “with all purity.”

Sometimes the children get fixed up first and go back home to that sinful family. The parents notice the righteous change and ask the reason of the hope that is in them: where did you learn this respect for me, when I have been nothing but a bad father or mother to you? Then those parents come in and become repentant mothers and fathers.

This is how the Lord keeps his word, “I will receive you”, and “will be a Father unto you”. The whole nation, men and women, elder mothers and elder brothers, becomes the family we all need, and when you marry, you carry it on to your children through your generations.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 10:4-6
thread.text: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)

classes.title: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.label: Psalms 85:11
precepts.why:
“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. You are at war right now in your spirit, with evil temptations pushed on every front: family members, school, work, even your own thoughts as you sit here. The weapons are not guns; the weapons are the commandments of God, and they are mighty.

Mighty to pull down what? Lies. That is what the Bible does; that is how we tear the lies down. We open up the Bible and swallow up the lies, like it says in the Psalms: “Truth shall spring out of the earth; and righteousness shall look down from heaven.” We open this Bible, and the lies are swallowed up.

So “Casting down imaginations” is casting down lies, “and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God”, and the knowledge of God is the law, the Bible. When you open this Bible and apply the commandments, you get rid of those impulsive, sinful thoughts and bring every thought “into captivity” under the obedience of Christ. That is how you walk straight past your temptation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 8:11
precepts.why:
The weapons of our warfare are the commandments. You are supposed to answer your impulses, your sinful temptations, with the commandments of God, and that is supposed to turn you from the door of temptation. If you understood that death is around the corner, you would listen to these laws.

But the wicked man thinks judgment is far off: “Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil.” Because the judgment is not immediate, his sick, evil mind is emboldened to commit evil and sin, and he leaves the commandments to the side. You had better recognize where you are.

That is the war inside you. The Lord isn't asking you to pick up a gun and go do something out there; he is asking you to get your mind right and set this mark in your head to change your behavior. We don't advocate anyone initiating aggression; if someone comes at you with a rope or a knife, you defend yourself. But the gung-ho brothers who can't wait for war can't even discipline their food. The war to win first is against the heart that sin makes bold.

precepts.label: 2 Esdras 14:13
precepts.why:
“And having in a readiness to revenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.” Some of our people can't wait: they want to be part of the war in the streets, casting out demons, getting their names on the Saturday night specials: brother, get a good angle of me, I want my video to go up Saturday. But here's the stipulation: when your obedience is fulfilled. That means there is no impediment left in your spirit to commit sin; you are walking straight in your spirit, your household, with your children, blameless. Then you can go out and correct your people.

That is what the Apocrypha says: “Now therefore set thine house in order, and reprove thy people”. First set your house in order. Your physical house can't be set in order if your spiritual house, meaning your damn head, is not in order. You haven't even checked your own wicked thoughts, your own actions, your own temptations, and you are trying to correct your wife, your son and your daughter.

Set your head in order; then you can set your house in order; then you can reprove your people. That is when your obedience is fulfilled, and you can revenge all disobedience, because you checked it first within yourself. We want to play warrior, to look good, while there are demons all up in us that we have not corrected yet.

thread.label: 2 Corinthians 11:3
thread.text: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.

classes.title: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.label: James 1:14
precepts.why:
Paul fears “lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted”. Satan is able to see what is within you, and that is what he attacks: not the stuff you are strong in, but the stuff you are weak in. “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” The temptation comes from something already within you.

So if you have a problem with wanting to be the head honcho, wanting to be over your husband, wanting to be the shot caller in control of how things go in the home, Satan plays with that, and you will look up and there will be a complete role reversal in your home. Subtle means pleasing to the senses in a mild or nuanced way. That little bit of power feels good: I decide what we eat around here, I put up the curtains, I picked this out. Then you start overstepping your bounds and do not even know it was Satan who set you up with the curtains. Sisters, when you start to overstep your divine place and purpose, say, that's Satan, you almost got me.

Most of us have been infected by the westernized mindset: birthdays, baby showers, Mother's Day and Father's Day, Thanksgiving, the ring on the finger, rules God did not make that we think are how life is supposed to be. The same goes for how a man deals with his wife. A father who told his son, get your money, the hoes are going to come, and left a condom on his dresser for him, normalized it. That residue has to be let go completely, or it will cloud your judgment and ruin your marriage.

It is the house of the man. Joshua said, as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord; he did not say, in agreement with my wife. He commanded his home. And some brothers take themselves out of that role and want to be a mama's boy in the marriage, wanting her to mother them instead of leading her. That emboldens her, and now you are her child and that is how she speaks to you. Both are drawn away by their own lust, and Satan works subtly on what is already within.

thread.label: Galatians 3:13
thread.text: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:

classes.title: False New Year: Doctrine Slayer - True Past Curses & Trauma

precepts.label: Acts 5:30
precepts.why:
Peter and the other apostles told our wicked elders, “We ought to obey God rather than men.” And then: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched.

Why does Peter call it a tree? What is the cross made of? Wood. Hanging on the cross is hanging on a tree. He says it again in Acts 10:39: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. Some say he was hanged from an actual tree, but Thomas said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” What would they need nails for on a tree? His hands and feet were nailed to a cross, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. And they mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” A man hanging by the neck from a tree could not be answering questions; he would be choking to death. So Peter called the crucifixion hanging on a tree, and the two men beside him were lynched too.

It is ironic: the same way the white man lynched us in slavery and into the 60s is the same way our King was killed. That is why Galatians 3:13 matters: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. Christ was hanged on a tree under the same curse as his people.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 21:23
precepts.why:
Hanging was our punishment too, in the law, for the wicked: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:” “His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled”.

That is what Paul quotes in Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. The curse of the law means its condemnation; being made a curse means being put to death for us, a sacrifice.

So what happened to our people? We were hanged on trees, because we went under the curses. Christ went under the curses of Deuteronomy 28 along with us, and we are under the curses too. He that is hanged is accursed of God: Christ was hanged on a tree, and so were we. The King and his children were hanged.

And the pattern keeps turning, like a ring. In Egypt, when Moses said, let my people go to serve God, Pharaoh called us idle and took away the straw but kept the tale of bricks, with a quota of 2,000 bricks; the records name Yupa son of Uriah, a Hebrew, 370 short. Here it was a quota of 200 or 500 pounds of cotton. The officers set over us, the black elites, pastors and politicians in the white man's pocket, turned on Moses and Aaron for making Pharaoh hate them. It is the same curse, the same judgment, until Christ, who bore the curse, redeems us from it.

thread.label: Galatians 6:7-8
thread.text: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

classes.title: Satan's Kiss To Your Demise

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 30:19
precepts.why:
The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:15
precepts.why:
“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 26:16
precepts.why:
“As the sun when it ariseth in the high heaven; so is the beauty of a good wife in the ordering of her house.” The way she sets it up and the way she does things: that is her beauty.

Ephesians 5 says “as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be to their own husbands in every thing.” Submitting “as unto the Lord” means listening to your husband as you would to Christ, and assisting him in what he wants. It is the house of the husband, the house of Abiel, not the house of Abiel and his wife. When you understand whose house it is, you understand whose desires set what the house is supposed to be. If he wants a sound home, give him a sound home; if he wants a clean house, give him a clean house. The confusion comes when a sister thinks her aspirations supersede his. We are on the same team, but somebody is the CEO of the team making the decisions for the franchise.

Be honest, sisters: in the ordering of the house, most husbands let you do pretty much what you want. I don’t give a damn about them pots. The drapes, the knives and forks, the couch set: most men are not tripping over that. As long as he comes home to good food and a clean house, however she got there is fine. So stop acting like submission is straight slavery; most of that is exaggeration. If she wants to lift the carpet and vacuum the cushion every morning, that is her ordering, and that is her beauty.

For the brothers whose wives do not want to clean except when company comes over, cleaning for presentation: you have to order your house. Tell her this is not the desire of your home, this is what needs to be done, and demand it. For the brothers with neat freaks, that is a blessing; sometimes you have to calm them down.

This is also what Titus 2 means by “keepers at home”: a good wife in the ordering of her house, not idle, not a busybody in everybody else’s house, taking care of home.

thread.label: Ephesians 5:22-33
thread.text: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.

classes.title: Respect: The Evidence Of Her Faith

precepts.label: Matthew 7:22-23
precepts.why:
“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.” The same respect you would show to Christ is the respect you should show your husband. There are going to be sisters who find out they are not going to get the kingdom because they did not respect nor reverence their husband. Some sisters said, damn, so we're going to go to hell because we're disrespectful? Yes. You didn't realize that?

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works?” They are going to have the audacity: Lord, I taught classes, I was out in the streets handing out flyers, I didn't eat pork, I left the shrimp alone, I wore fringes every day. “And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

What could keep them from knowing the Lord? Iniquity: sin. Sister, every command your husband gives you is law. It is like getting orders from God for you. As long as your husband is not asking you to sin, if he asks you to do something, it is sin if you don't do it.

In the westernized mindset that doesn't compute: he has that much power? You malfunction because you don't believe he is a god; you don't see the Christ in him. You had better read your Bible. He absolutely has that much authority over you, and all the wonderful works in the world will not cover the iniquity of disrespecting him.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 5:8
precepts.why:
When Ephesians 5 is read, some think there's wiggle room: that doesn't really mean that. This makes complete sense on the brothers' side of the room: “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.”

Provide means her food, her raiment, her clothing. Lord, I didn't eat pork, I didn't eat shrimp or lobster, I stopped dealing with the prostitutes, I kept the Sabbath day holy. But you didn't take care of your wife or your kids. You were a deadbeat; you did nothing for her; you left the house, living among everybody else doing what you wanted, saying, I'm not dealing with that woman no more. That was your wife. That man has denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel. Is that man going to see the kingdom? No.

“Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church”. Is that an option? If I don't do that, will I see the kingdom? The natural thing for the evil man on this side of the earth is to be promiscuous, to roam, with nothing holding him down. Is that love? No.

So what makes you think it's any different when a wife doesn't submit? Your level of faith is shown by the level of respect you have for your husband, because that is the level of respect you have for God. The same goes for the man: the way you love and care for your wife is the level of love you have for Christ. If you don't love, protect and provide for her, you're an infidel; if you don't respect your husband and do what he says, you're an infidel. Fringes and every Sabbath don't matter.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:13
precepts.why:
“let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.” There is no room for options there. Nowhere does the scripture say you can respect him as long as he does this or that. If that's in your mind, you're led by the damn devil. Nobody says, I won't eat pork unless; I'll keep the Sabbath day if. No.

Your whole duty in life: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” There is no excuse for not observing a commandment.

Now, if you are being beaten in a relationship, are we telling you to stay, sister? No. If he's beating you to a pulp, get away from him. Don't die, sister. He obviously isn't keeping the commandments if he's harming you. But if he is not asking you to sin, you do not have a reason. You show him through your chaste conversation and your actions that you are going to serve the Lord no matter what; you heap hot coals on his head.

Disrespect should never be an option. Only Satan gives you that option. If submission depends on his behavior, it isn't submission; it's manipulation. God told you to submit without a caveat, because it is a commandment, and keeping the commandments is the whole duty.

precepts.label: Colossians 3:18
precepts.why:
Paul addresses it in almost all of his writings: “Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as it is fit in the Lord.” What is fit in the Lord? As the Lord has designed. Can you truly say you are in the truth and not respect that man? You can't, no matter how long you have been sitting here.

We understand that, just as we men have residue from the world to beat, our wives do too; they are the weaker vessel, and Satan often comes through the woman to destroy the house. So we have to dwell with them according to knowledge and cast down every imagination with the scriptures. Sisters, your toughest plight in this truth is going to be honoring your husband. You tolerate all those folks at the job and listen to the boss; your husband is supposed to get many times more respect than him, and you never clock out. Even your anatomy tells you that you are to be submissive; it's the world telling you that you have options.

Reverence is deep respect for someone or something. Respect is deep admiration: esteem, regard, admiration, veneration, awe. That is what you are to have for your husband, even if he snores or limps when he walks, because you chose him. Imagine arguing with Christ: you can't even put that together in your mind. If he says park the car in that spot, it's law.

And if you only knew: a righteous man will do almost anything to see you happy. The Deacon's daughter Mimi comes running to the door, Daddy!, and she can get anything from him; she knows her role and plays it well. If you want, you've got to be a princess. Reverence him, make him feel he is everything he's supposed to be, and watch what happens. Get your spirit right, and you'll see that Ephesians 5 man you want.

thread.label: Ephesians 5:22-25,32-33
thread.text: Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord.

classes.title: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 7:28
precepts.why:
Paul says plainly: “But and if thou marry, thou hast not sinned; and if a virgin marry, she hath not sinned. Nevertheless such shall have trouble in the flesh.” Marriage is no sin, but there will be trouble in it. Every marriage meets conflict.

How a couple deals with that trouble depends on the expectations they carried into it. Scripture does not define marriage by feelings; it defines it by function. Marriage originated with God. Culture later added the ceremonies, made it a business, and put unrealistic expectations on it. The traditions may carry meaning, but they do not replace the original design. That is the modern confusion: putting feelings in front of function.

So the trouble in the flesh is expected, and it is met with the order of Ephesians 5: the husband as the head who gives himself for the wife, the wife submitting “as unto the Lord.” Marriage is meant to function first, and through aging together the feelings do what they do.

precepts.label: Sirach 26:2
precepts.why:
“A virtuous woman rejoiceth her husband, and he shall fulfil the years of his life in peace.” The Bible calls for peace in the marriage: not war, not strife, not enmity, not division, not variance.

This is how the trouble in the flesh of 1 Corinthians 7:28 is handled. The wife focuses on rejoicing her husband through reverence, and then he stands in his integrity, because there is peace in the household. Peace, not passion. Peace, not feelings.

That reverence is what Ephesians 5:33 asks: “the wife see that she reverence her husband.” Reverence is beyond respect. It is a profound, heartfelt attitude of awe, that manifests as obedience and submission. It cannot be done as a job description; it has to come from the heart, and if a sister does not have that spirit she has to pray for it. When it comes from genuine respect and a desire to please the Lord, she will not be derelict in her duties, and the house has peace.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 11:2-3
precepts.why:
Paul praises the brethren that they “keep the ordinances, as I delivered them to you.” Then he gives the summary of the order: “the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.”

This is the same order as Ephesians 5:23: “the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.” The woman’s list of duties may look longer, but the man’s responsibilities carry much more weight, because he is the one that is accountable. A sister’s accountability is for herself; the husband is accountable for her, the house, the children and the nation. He is the saviour of the body. Does that not deserve honour?

When marriage is grounded in the order God established, love becomes stronger. The passion and the joy come, not romance, which is a new modern term, but the more meaningful feelings behind it, and the marriage becomes more durable over time. Marriage mirrors Christ and the Israelites, and prophecy is not entertainment: it is a sign for us to correct ourselves and get things in order, individually and as a people.

precepts.label: Galatians 6:2
precepts.why:
“Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.” If I esteem you better than myself, then within my power I have to help you come up with a solution, or help provide it. “Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.” That does not mean just looking: yeah, he's struggling like hell. No. Look means action. “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus.” And Christ was no weak, effeminate man; he was a strong, powerful, upright man.

Paul says it plainly: “Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.” That is how we are going to rise. If twelve of you have cars that run fine and a brother in the body can't even fix his car, and you shut your mouth and do nothing, you are weak. That is not how our black men are supposed to stand. Israelites are commanded to help each other.

So every school should have its mechanics, carpenters, plumbers and electricians helping the people in the body, making videos so the next brother can do it too. Instead of paying $1,900 you pay $300 for the parts, and brothers with the spirit fix the car. That's alms deeds; that's helping your nation.

We used to have that. Black people used to speak to each other in the street because we had a commonality, a common struggle. Now we have fallen apart. Bearing one another's burdens is how the nation is gathered together and becomes an economic force: that is the mind of Christ and the law of Christ.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 7:12
precepts.why:
Looking on the things of others means building something together, and economics must be part of our mindset as we walk to build a nation. Solomon says: “For wisdom is a defence, and money is a defence: but the excellency of knowledge is, that wisdom giveth life to them that have it.”

Wisdom is a defence: generational wisdom passed down from father to son, grandfather to son. Esau has law in his house, and the grandfather passes the torch and teaches hard lessons that save heartache; that is why they had the head start, and why they are so relaxed at their jobs. We are behind in everything. Half of black folks have a credit score below 620, locked out of access to capital; before we wake up in the morning, half of us are in bondage.

Money is a defence. Walking the commandments, evil is going to come upon you: what happens when they take your job? So build businesses we can self-employ in, food distribution, brothers helping each other. Teach your children about secured loans and secured credit cards and the three credit bureaus, Experian, TransUnion and Equifax. And a single, divorced brother paying out his money has less of a defence than a man married in proper order.

“wisdom giveth life to them that have it”, and to have it you have to be taught it. That is why they try to stop us from teaching that we are the twelve tribes of Israel: scattered, we lost our nationality, heritage and commandments. The father in the house, with Christ at his head, is the one to break that cycle.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 36:25
precepts.why:
“Where no hedge is, there the possession is spoiled.” A bishop must be “One that ruleth well his own house”, and a man who will not lead his house has no hedge around it. If you don’t lead your house, you are going to lose control, and your possession, your wife, will be spoiled.

Failure to lead is one of the things husbands do that destroy marriages. Not stepping up, not taking control of your home, being a passive individual while your wife walks all over you. Eventually some other man is going to come along who catches her eye, and she is going to desire and look to him. Coach Dingolane destroyed a house that way, all because a man would not step up and lead his home.

The flock of God’s pasture are men, and leaders are men. If you are not there guiding, not there instructing, not there correcting, the marriage will come to a crashing halt with her standing over you.

That is why Paul asks, “For if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?” How can you lead other men and tell them this is the way, if your own house is out of order, if your wife doesn’t listen to you and your kids don’t listen to you? You cannot be over men if you are not able to rule your own house. And the qualities of a bishop are for every man: a bishop is an example of what we are all supposed to be.

precepts.label: 1 Peter 3:7
precepts.why:
“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel.” Failure to dwell with his wife according to knowledge is another of the things husbands do that destroy marriages, and ruling your own house well depends on it.

A wise husband studies his wife: her fears, her emotions, her struggles, her strengths. That is dwelling with her according to knowledge. When you understand your wife, you are able to guide your house. You push her toward greatness, but you also know her limits, and because you know them you set things up in the home so that things can work. If your wife is emotionally not there to deal with certain things, then you set it up another way. In order to lead, you have to know what they deal with, what they are able to do and what they are not able to do. That goes for your kids as well. You do it now without realizing it: you understand strengths and weaknesses, and you prioritize based on that.

Some men never learn their wives and then wonder why the marriage feels distant.

The other things that destroy a house show the same failure to know her: bitterness and harshness, holding things over her after she has repented and humiliating her, when you are supposed to love your wife as your own self; neglect, when a trip to Walmart is an exciting event for her because you haven’t taken her out, while ordering the house and dealing with the kids all the time is difficult; and withholding love and affection, because if she is not getting it from you, where is she going to get it from? A bishop rules his own house well by dwelling with his wife according to knowledge and giving her honour.

precepts.label: Hebrews 7:14
precepts.why:
“Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same.” The children are the disciples, us, and Christ took part of the same flesh and blood. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham”, which is flesh and blood. “Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.” In all things, not some things. How is a man made like his brethren in all things? By having a father and a mother.

Then Hebrews 7: “For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.” He sprang out of Judah based on his father. The tribe comes from the father, as every Israelite’s does.

The fathers show the same. God told David, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels.” David knew “that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne.” And Paul says Christ “was made of the seed of David according to the flesh.” According to the flesh: made flesh and blood like his brethren.

That is why Matthew says “When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” Coming together was the customary wedding feast, as when Laban “made a feast” and Jacob went in unto his wife. Joseph and Mary were already espoused, and betrothal is marriage, so there was no fornication; they lay together before the feast. Child of the Holy Ghost means child of prophecy, the prophecy made to David. Joseph, a just man, was “not willing to make her a publick example”, which means stoned to death, and “was minded to put her away privily”: to hide her, because the child was his. Why would a just man hide a woman for something he did not do? And the angel called him “Joseph, thou son of David.” So our Lord sprang out of Judah through his father, made like his brethren in all things.

thread.text: Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account, that they may do it with joy, and not with grief: for that is unprofitable for you.

classes.title: Why Do Fools Fall In Love

precepts.label: Proverbs 11:14
precepts.why:
“Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls.” Watching for your souls is a job. Leadership is not about sitting in the front and getting the plates first. There are things you never see, never hear about and never have to deal with, because there are things put in place: the men who deal with the men, whose phones are the first ones to get called, and the senior sisters who deal with the sisters.

“Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.” If you don’t follow counsel, you will fall. A congregation without counsel will fall; there is no way around it.

You have all the wisdom and understanding in front of you. If something is said to you on the phone, you can say hold on, I’ll call you right back, and reach out to a senior brother or senior sister: does this sound right? And they will tell you: no, that doesn’t sound right; no, you can’t do that; no, that’s not wise. You can alleviate a lot of situations that way. But for some reason everybody is grown: oh, I can deal with it. No, you are not in your right mind, obviously. Because of lust you ignore all the red flags, and every red flag you see before you get married is heightened a thousand times after, because you are with them every single day.

The protocol is part of that safety. No brothers should be dealing with the women on any counseling basis. The senior sisters are set up to deal with the women, and if it is a congregational issue, or somebody has to be judged, the senior sisters bring it to leadership and it is dealt with there. That multitude of counsellors is how leadership watches for your soul.

precepts.label: Sirach 32:19
precepts.why:
“Do nothing without advice; and when thou hast once done, repent not.” The ones who watch for your souls give the counsel, and you are not to move without it. Sisters, you have been given the blueprint, the things to look for when it comes to men.

When looking for a husband, you are trying to identify stability and discipline. “He that hath no rule over his own spirit is like a city that is broken down, and without walls.” He is not stable; how is he going to take care of you? He is blown about with every wind of doctrine, bringing out little dumb breakdowns that did not come from leadership, like mashed potatoes on the Passover. Red flag. “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: one minute it’s this, the next minute it’s that. Spiritually you should never aim down; aim up for a man with more understanding than you, who can lead and guide you. If you marry a novice and you are the one teaching him to wear fringes every day, you lose respect for him, and you have married down. And don’t think you are going to change him; men typically do not look to you for counsel.

“But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel.” A brother barely able to feed himself, getting kicked out of apartments, lights cut off, staying at his cousin’s house, is not ready for a wife, and you are not stepping in to save a negro. Spot the signs of lust: a brother telling you at 11 p.m. that he is naked is setting the mood and lining you up. Get the hell off the phone and put him in his place. And ask leadership how he handles correction: “he that hateth reproof is brutish”, and a man who cannot take correction from the men over him has a problem with God.

If you see these signs early, congratulations, sister, you spotted him. Now are you going to play dumb because you like the idea of being married, or wise up and follow counsel? Do nothing without advice, and once you have done it with advice, you will not have to repent of it. Break the cycle.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:1-5
precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.” You are going to be tried. Sirach tells you to get ready for it: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight, and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have demons in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back, and you have to be able to fight and get away from them. Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take it away, and the Lord said no, this is the thorn in your side; this is what you will have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our lives, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships and with one another.

“and make not haste in time of trouble.” Things are going to happen, and you can’t fold up; go full-fledged toward it and knock it out. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it victorious and on top. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. For gold is tried in the fire.”

You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point. Everything in the world is against the person trying to be righteous: the work schedule set up to keep you in sin on the weekend, the holidays you want off based on wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable. That is the man who endures temptation and receives the crown of life.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is some attraction there, something that makes us gravitate toward the elements in us that cause us to sin. It seduces us: it looks like it is right for us, but it is not. Paul warned of it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits.”

A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you. Like drugs: that crack feels real good to the crackhead, but he is not able to see around him, and his whole life is being destroyed.

The only way you are going to see whether it is good for you or not is by filtering it through the scriptures. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back. You have to be in the spirit to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss.

Temptation begins internally; the lust is in you. When temptation presents itself you begin to be drawn to it, sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed, then you agree with it. “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” It becomes action, and it always ends in destruction. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” In your own counsel you will always think you are right, and that is how people give heed to seducing spirits and depart from the faith.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 7:26
precepts.why:
“Hast thou a wife after thy mind? forsake her not”. Very few understand that this is not their show. It is about the house of her husband. A wife after your mind is a woman who understands that she is in subjection to you and that you are the head of the home, so what you want is what she wants. She makes your desires her desires. Your aspirations become her aspirations. How you want things to be becomes how she wants things to be, because she understands her desire is unto her husband, not unto herself.

If her husband wants the environment this way, she makes the environment that way. If he wants the household this way, she makes the household this way. That is her job as the manager of the house: to make sure the CEO is happy. That is what a woman is supposed to do. But the world told her, no, it's yours, sis, you do what you want to do.

That is the last of the ten signs that she does not respect the Christ in you: she does not follow your lead spiritually, does not align with your direction in this truth, and picks and chooses what to follow. A wife after your mind is the opposite, and that is the wife Peter speaks of. By being in subjection to her own husband, her chaste conversation can win even a man that obeys not the word. The one who used to be loud and argue now does what he asks without challenging his authority, and he says, the word did that? Let me go see what those brothers in purple and gold are talking about.

Through submission you can move mountains with a man. When she knows she is right and still stands down because he is the head and has the final say, he is left with hot coals on his head, knowing she is more righteous than he is. It changes a man. That is a wife not to forsake.

precepts.label: Revelation 13:17
precepts.why:
Tobit had a decent job in captivity, over the king’s accounts, and while he was well off he did good: “I gave many alms to my brethren, and gave my bread to the hungry, And my clothes to the naked”. When Sennacherib came back from Judea, where an angel killed 185,000 of his men, he came back mad and took it out on Ephraim, throwing them off the walls. Tobit would sneak and bury them: “I buried them privily”. He was not supposed to; the king wanted to see those bodies, “but the bodies were not found, when they were sought for of the king.”

Then he got ratted out: “when one of the Ninevites went and complained of me to the king, that I buried them”, he knew he “was sought for to be put to death” and became a fugitive. “Then all my goods were forcibly taken away, neither was there any thing left me, beside my wife Anna and my son Tobias.” Everything he had, they took from him.

That is what Revelation 13 means when it says no man should buy or sell. All the positions and things you have here: the time is going to come when you go against this system, teach against it, and do not support the beast, and everything you have they will take from you. Tobit is the example. They took his possessions, and most likely his wife and child were taken too, imprisoned, because he was considered an enemy of the state. That is the consequence for serving God, and the time is coming when you will have to make the choice to serve God.

But the Lord spared his son and wife. Within fifty-five days Sennacherib’s own sons killed him, and Sarchedonus set Tobit’s nephew Achiacharus over the accounts. “And Achiacharus intreating for me, I returned to Nineve.” His nephew was cupbearer, “keeper of the signet, and steward, and overseer of the accounts”, next unto the king, and he spoke for his uncle. Then “my wife Anna was restored unto me, with my son Tobias, in the feast of Pentecost”: he was keeping the feasts in captivity, not in Jerusalem.

Tobit stayed faithful, and he was not alone out there being righteous. He looked out for his people with the status he had, fed the hungry and gave alms to those keeping the commandments in captivity, and when it came back around his nephew did the same for him. The Lord looked out for him as he looked out for his own people.
